description: Set off on a journey through the Pacific Islands while armed with the legendary IMAGI-TOOL 2000 (a.k.a. a pool noodle). Also, on stage will be a retelling of a classic fable, “Little Red Riding Hood and the Dragon” by Ying Chang Compenstine. title: Does Your Lover Feel Distant? This Fixed Mine
description:
For weeks, I felt like a stranger in my own relationship. He stopped calling like he used to, barely responded to texts, and when we were together, it felt like he was a million miles away. I tried everything — heart-to-heart talks, giving him space, even ignoring him — but nothing worked… until I tried something different.

Out of frustration, I turned to a spiritual solution I had only heard whispers about. I scanned a code that promised emotional reconnection through energy work and ancient love rituals. Within hours, he messaged me with warmth I hadn’t felt in months.

If your partner feels emotionally distant or cold, don’t ignore that feeling. You deserve answers — and real change.

owner.name: Spelman College Museum of Fine Art

name: Amanda Williams: We Say What Black This Is
title: Amanda Williams: We Say What Black This Is
description:
Spelman College Museum of Fine Art presents We Say What Black This Is, an exhibition showcasing mixed media and watercolor paintings by MacArthur award-winning artist Amanda Williams. The new exhibit opens February 7, 2025, and will be on view through May 24, 2025.

We Say What Black This Is celebrates the diversity, resilience and depth of Blackness while challenging simplistic definitions of Black identity. The exhibition features works from Williams' series What Black is this, You Say?, created in response to the ‘Blackout Tuesday’ social media moment in 2020. The exhibit will include a new abstract painting by Williams and student-written didactic labels.
venue: Spelman College Museum of Fine Art, 350 Spelman Lane, Camille Olivia Hanks Cosby Academic Center, Atlanta, GA 30314

name: Signs of the Times: The Changing Face of Football
title:
Signs of the Times: The
Changing Face of Football
description:
The College Football Hall of Fame recently unveiled its newest limited-time exhibit, which offers visitors an inside look into the complex history of on-field communication devices. Titled “Signs of the Times,” the exhibit is an immersive experience that explores the evolution of how coaches communicate with their team on the field, from early face-to-face instructions and hand signals, to today’s high-tech innovations.

Some highlights of the exhibit include:

- A Transparent Football Helmet displaying Coach-to-Player Receivers on loan from CoachComm
- An entire X-System Sideline Cart on loan from CoachComm
- Interactive Playboard Game for fans to guess the play call

The exhibit is currently available through the month of May, and can be found on the second floor of the Hall of Fame, in the Andrea & James Clarke Family Gallery.
venue: College Football Hall of Fame, 250 Marietta St NW, Atlanta, GA 30313

description:

After successfully providing financial aid to five outstanding individuals last year, the program is again looking to fund five scholarships of $5,000 each to high school seniors planning to attend or students currently enrolled at a Historically Black College and University.

Visit the Hall of Fame website for more details. Applications will be accepted through May 31, 2025.
